title: Patients
meta: View or manage the patient index
intro: Find the patient records received with lab data, read their identifiers and requests, and review possible duplicates. The Patients page reads source records. It does not offer patient editing or merging.
Patient settings are optional. OpenLDR receives patients with lab data before you label identifier systems. We strongly recommend adding useful labels and reviewing possible duplicates during use.
Use your own received records and identifier systems. No documentation sample data is required. The pictures show fictional patients in a test installation. Optional practice data is at the end.

View patient index allows a masked list and exact-identifier searches. View patient identifiers allows full names, identifiers, dates of birth and contact details, plus name searches. These unmasked views are audited. The pictures use this permission.
Manage patient index allows identifier-system settings and duplicate decisions. A lab receiving identifier labels from central cannot change those shared labels here.

tasks.title: Find a patient and read their details
intro: Use this when you need to check who a source record describes and which lab requests belong to it. If the list is empty, return after your normal feed has sent patient data.
steps: Select Patients in the main menu, then use the Patients tab.
In Search name or identifier, enter a name or identifier. Without permission to view identifiers, the field reads Exact identifier and requires the complete identifier value.
Read the name, sex, age, listed identifiers and request count. Match the person using your source records. Names alone do not establish identity.
Select the row. Identity in the Patient sheet shows source details. The row dots menu also offers View.
Under Identifiers, read each identifier system and value. A system label changes the display name, not the source value.
Under Requests, check the order dates, panels, requesting facilities, statuses and result counts. Use the request pagination if there are more rows.
Select Close at the top right to return to the list.
tasks.result: You can inspect the record without changing patient details. Corrections to source identity data belong in the system that maintains it.

tasks.title: Name an identifier system and show it in the list
intro: An identifier system is the URI that says what kind of identifier a value is. Configure systems that have arrived from your data sources. Use a label people recognise.
steps: Select Identifier systems at the top of Patients. It lists received systems and patient counts.
Open the dots on the correct system row and select Edit. Check the URI before changing its settings.
In Label, enter the readable name. The fictional example uses Example ID. Leave it blank to use the source-provided name.
Choose whether to show its values
Turn on Show in the list to include this system in the Patients table's Identifiers column.
Check whether searches should match it
Keep Search matches it on for useful identifying values. Turn it off for a placeholder system that should not identify a person. It also affects same-identifier duplicate matching.
Select the dots in this settings sheet.
tasks.result: The system row shows its saved label and display/search settings.

tasks.title: Find a patient by a listed identifier
intro: Search by the identifier value, not the label. More than one matching record can appear when the source contains a shared or duplicated identifier.
steps: Select Patients and enter the identifier value. The example searches DOCS-001.
Read the Identifiers column. This example shows Example ID: DOCS-001. The two fictional records deliberately share it.
tasks.result: Matching patients appear with the configured identifier label. An empty Identifiers column does not mean the source record has no identifiers; check the display setting.

tasks.title: Find records marked Merged
intro: Use this when the source has made a record inactive or reported a replacement. The default patient list shows active records.
steps: Use Status as the column and keep Equals.
tasks.result: The list shows records marked Merged. A badge appears beside their names. Clear the status filter when you want active records again.

tasks.title: Follow a replacement reported by the source
intro: A replaced record can point to the patient it was merged into upstream. OpenLDR follows that reported link; this action does not merge records.
steps: Select the merged patient row. A reported replacement adds an actions menu in its Identity section.
Select Open the patient this record was merged into.
tasks.result: The replacement patient opens in the read-only Patient sheet.

tasks.title: Inspect a possible duplicate group
intro: Review the evidence before deciding whether records describe the same person. A shared identifier can be a data-entry problem or a placeholder. OpenLDR does not resolve that decision for you.
steps: Select Duplicates at the top of Patients.
Check why each group was suggested and how many patients it contains. The example matches a shared identifier.
Select the group row to open Likely duplicates.
Read the evidence, identifiers and available identity details. Same-name matching also requires matching birth details and compatible sex values.
Use that member's dots menu and select Open patient to inspect its full record and requests.
tasks.result: The selected member opens in a read-only Patient sheet. No patient record is merged by reviewing the group.

tasks.title: Record that a group contains different people
intro: Only use this after checking that the suggested records are different people. For an actual duplicate, correct the source records instead. The group decision is reversible.
steps: If a member's Patient sheet is open, select Close to return to Likely duplicates.
In Reason, record why these are different people. The example explicitly describes its fictional demonstration.
Select the dots beside the group's Evidence heading.
Mark the group as different people
tasks.result: The group disappears from Open. Patient records remain unchanged.

tasks.title: Show a reviewed group again
intro: Use this to undo a previous Not duplicates decision and return the group for review.
steps: In Duplicates, open Status and choose Not duplicates.
Open the group dots menu and select Show again.
tasks.result: The group is back in the open review list.

tasks.title: Export open duplicate groups
intro: Use this when the team maintaining the source records needs the open groups. Export requires View patient identifiers and is audited.
steps: Select the dots above the Duplicates table.
Select Export CSV. The browser downloads the open groups.
tasks.result: The CSV includes the identifiers needed for source review. The export does not mark or merge any patient.

tasks.title: Use Patients on a phone
intro: The tabs and patient sheet remain available on a phone. A wide list can scroll horizontally.
steps: Use Patients, Identifier systems or Duplicates at the top.
Use the search field, with the same identifier permissions as on desktop.
Select the matching row and scroll the Patient sheet to read its sections.

end.title: Optional practice with fictional patients
paragraphs: Every task above can use your received records. This optional file is only for a test installation. It contains three fictional patient records, one request, one report and one result. Two patient records share an identifier; one old record points to its replacement.
Download the six-resource practice bundle. Read Start here for installed and development CLI instructions, then put the file in your installation's data folder.
html:
Development checkout example:

cd ~/Downloads/openldr_ce
pnpm openldr ingest data/example-patients.json

For an installed Linux or macOS copy, use ./openldr instead of pnpm openldr. On Windows, use .\openldr.ps1 from your installation folder, such as C:\openldr_ce. Replace example folders with your real folder. Start here shows each platform.
The fixture does not require the optional Test catalog practice files. Request and patient counts in your installation can differ from the pictures.

end.title: Understand masking and duplicate limits
paragraphs: Without View patient identifiers, names are masked, identifiers show only their last four characters, and birth dates show only the year. Phone and email are hidden. Search requires an exact identifier. These limits also apply when inspecting duplicate groups.

Same-identifier groups use the same value in the same searchable identifier system. Identifiers with no system and systems with Search matches it off are excluded. Name-and-birth-date matching ignores case, spacing and accents. Active records are compared.
A group shows at most 50 members. A larger group cannot be marked here. Check whether a placeholder identifier has been used for many people and correct the source data or searchable-system setting.
Patient data belongs to the source workflow. This page reads identity records, labels identifier systems and records duplicate-review decisions. It has no patient-edit or merge action.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: The patient list is empty. Check whether patient data has arrived from your normal feed. You do not need sample data or identifier labels to receive patients.
Part of a name finds nothing. A user without View patient identifiers must search the complete identifier value. Check Search matches it for that identifier system.
The Identifiers column is empty. Enable Show in the list for a received system. Open the Patient sheet to check the source identifiers themselves.
Identifier settings cannot be edited. Check Manage patient index and whether the labels come from central. A central-managed lab reads those labels here.
The sheet says the list is out of date. Reload the page and reopen the patient. The list reference can expire after a server restart.
A duplicate group returns after a source update. Compare the current membership and evidence. Correct actual duplicates in the source system rather than marking them as different people.
